title: Special Board Meeting
blurb: The board approved a modified end-of-year schedule and family support for Kaler Elementary's closure, while also approving an interim superintendent, a significant retirement contribution, and acknowledging a director's resignation.

title: Executive Session & Special Meeting
blurb: The board approved Dr. Angela Atkinson-Dena as superintendent and, following extensive debate and an initial defeat, passed a plan to reassign Kaler Elementary students with provisions for waivers and transportation. Eight staff resignations were also reported, and public comment included transportation and Kaler reassignment concerns.

title: May Regular Meeting
blurb: The board authorized contract negotiations for a preferred superintendent candidate and committed to investigating significant bus overcrowding concerns, alongside approving staff contracts, discussing elementary reconfiguration, and reviewing financial updates.

title: Special Meeting
blurb: The school board finalized the FY2027 budget with a 6% tax impact after extensive discussion on personnel cuts and financial stability. Following passionate public debate, the board voted 5-1 to delay the elementary school reconfiguration until the 2027-28 school year, committing to a detailed planning process.

title: April Regular Meeting
blurb: The Board voted to halt the elementary school reconfiguration for 2026-2027 and unanimously approved a 1% tax increase to seed the contingency fund, addressing an anticipated FY27 deficit. They also narrowed the superintendent search to two finalists and discussed the Kaler closure's impact.

title: Special Budget Meeting
blurb: The Board of Education adopted the FY27 budget 4-2, utilizing unexpected health insurance savings to reinstate positions and build contingency, amidst significant public opposition to the elementary reconfiguration plan and concerns over special education staffing.

title: Special Budget Meeting
blurb: The school board reviewed the FY27 budget, which includes a 6.0% tax increase and staffing changes, amidst strong community opposition to school reconfiguration and cuts to student-facing positions. They also removed a controversial early release proposal and will seek budgetary guidance from the City Council.

title: Board Workshop — Non-Biased Training for Hiring
Special Budget Meeting
blurb: The Board voted to close Kaler Elementary and reconfigure remaining schools into a new grade model, but rejected the Superintendent's FY2027 budget due to concerns over significant personnel cuts and process, scheduling a special meeting for further deliberation.

title: Budget Workshop II
blurb: The school board presented a budget to address a significant financial crisis, proposing a 6% tax increase, 12% staff reduction, Kaler Elementary closure, and district restructuring, which drew community concern over the impact on student-facing positions and special education services.

title: March Regular Meeting
blurb: The school board discussed an FY2027 budget proposal featuring significant reductions, including 77 positions and the closure of Dyer Elementary, necessitated by a depleted fund balance. Both board members and the public voiced strong concerns regarding the cuts' magnitude and the rapid decision-making timeline.

title: Budget Workshop I
blurb: Facing $7-8 million in budget cuts, the SPSD board discussed elementary school reconfiguration scenarios, including school closures, to address declining enrollment and equity. However, board members and the public strongly opposed closing Skillin Elementary due to significant equity concerns and negative community impacts.

title: February Regular Meeting
blurb: The board addressed a significant FY2027 budget shortfall, exacerbated by school nutrition fund deficits and audit findings, by exploring elementary school reconfiguration and expanding the Community School model. The superintendent search is underway with student participation, and the board also endorsed a resolution supporting the local immigrant community.

title: January Regular Meeting
blurb: The board addressed a projected budget deficit and announced a public forum for the difficult FY2027 budget, while also approving a contract for the superintendent search. Significant concerns were raised regarding recent ICE activity, and the SPHS 2026 graduation was moved offsite.

title: Board Workshop — Robert's Rules of Order
Board Preliminary Budget Workshop
blurb: The school board began its FY2027 budget process, directing the administration to draft a budget based on a 6.5% tax increase due to declining enrollment and financial shortfalls. They also discussed major cost-saving proposals, including elementary school reconfiguration, and announced upcoming public workshops for the superintendent search and community engagement.

title: Board Workshop and Special Meeting
blurb: The school board reviewed proposals from three superintendent search firms, debating their costs and approaches. Despite concerns over its higher price, the board voted 4-2 to hire Zeal Education Group, contingent on positive reference checks.

title: December Regular Meeting
blurb: The board ratified a new contract with SPESPA, but also addressed a projected $1.3-1.9 million FY25 budget deficit by implementing an immediate non-personnel spending freeze. Other actions included welcoming new members, scheduling a superintendent search workshop, and accepting over $46,000 in donations.

title: November Regular Meeting
blurb: The board ratified the teachers' collective bargaining agreement and discussed a budget deficit, partially offset by a geothermal tax credit, while warning of critical fund balance depletion. They also addressed significant remediation plans for the middle school field and approved a concussion policy.

title: September Regular Meeting
blurb: The board discussed significant financial concerns, including payroll errors, a depleted fund balance, and an upcoming audit, also sending a concussion policy back for revision. Updates included a positive school year start, new nutrition initiatives, and a slight enrollment decrease.

title: July Regular Meeting
blurb: The board approved a superintendent transition and elected a new chair, while also addressing a potential budget deficit and outlining a proactive AI strategy for the district. The district reported strong staffing for the upcoming year and ongoing summer facilities projects.

title: Special Meeting
blurb: The school board initiated a search for an interim superintendent and authorized a separation agreement with Superintendent Metheny, while also approving a tentative agreement with SPESPA and thanking voters for passing the school budget.

title: June Regular Meeting
blurb: The school board announced Superintendent Metheny's resignation and a transition plan, while highlighting significant district progress, planned security upgrades, and a new pre-K partnership, despite a decrease in federal funding, urging public support for the upcoming budget referendum.

title: Special Meeting
blurb: The school board approved the FY2026 budget articles totaling $73,131,556, including a $3.9M capital plan, with one article passing 4-2 due to social-emotional learning funding concerns. The Superintendent also announced three resignations.

title: Special Meeting
blurb: The school board reviewed an audit revealing material weaknesses and overspending, outlining corrective actions, and heard extensive public comment advocating for two special education teachers' contract renewals. The meeting also recognized the SPHS Robotics Team, noted positive SPHS academic and attendance progress, and approved various contracts and new administrative job descriptions.

title: Budget Adoption & Superintendent Evaluation
blurb: The board welcomed a new member, approved two hires and a cost-saving HR position, and announced three teacher resignations, clarifying they were not due to a reduction in force. They also reminded the community about the June 10th budget referendum and entered executive session.

title: Special Meeting
blurb: The board honored departing and welcomed new student representatives while approving several personnel changes, including a new Finance Director. Discussions also centered on the upcoming school budget referendum, with clarification that athletic complex improvements are a separate funding matter.

title: FY2026 Budget Workshop
blurb: The school board rescinded its prior decision on the SPHS athletic complex, approving a recommendation for a November 2025 ballot referendum with two conflicting bond questions for natural grass ($4.66M) or synthetic turf ($5.49M) options due to updated cost estimates. This action was taken despite mixed public comment and a potential state law conflict regarding required board recommendations on the ballot.

title: Special Meeting
blurb: The school board reviewed a proposed 5.98% budget increase for FY2026 that drew significant criticism for being 'top-heavy,' cutting student-facing and curriculum leadership positions while retaining administrative roles, and generated controversy over the Superintendent's communication with teachers.

title: Budget Workshop III and Special Meeting
blurb: The school board reviewed a proposed $73 million budget, which included some restorations, and debated further additions like SEL teachers. However, deep divisions over funding mechanisms, particularly a contentious salary freeze proposal, prevented any consensus or vote, leading to adjournment and a rescheduled meeting.

title: Budget Workshop II and Special Meeting
blurb: The school board navigated a challenging FY2025 budget, making difficult personnel cuts and restorations—including saving an Assistant Principal position and reducing 'second lunch' funding—to offset a new $200,000 health insurance deficit and keep the tax impact below 6%. They also addressed a DEI inquiry and funded the SPHS Robotics team's World Championship trip.

title: Budget Workshop I
blurb: The Superintendent presented a FY2026 budget requesting a 6% operating increase and $3.17 million more from taxpayers, despite significant staff reductions driven by declining enrollment and increased staffing since 2017. Community members strongly opposed cuts to student-facing roles, while the Superintendent acknowledged the high tax burden on residents.

title: March Regular Meeting
blurb: The board celebrated student achievements and approved a pre-kindergarten expansion. However, the proposed FY2026 budget, featuring a 5.98% increase and over 20 FTE position cuts, generated significant public concern regarding its impact on students and the budget process.

title: Strategic Plan Mid-Year Review
blurb: The Board addressed a challenging FY2026 budget context, anticipating position reductions, and voted 4-3 to recommend a November 2025 referendum for the SPHS athletic complex with two options. A new state-funded pre-K partnership was also announced.

title: State of the Schools
blurb: The board debated options for the South Portland High School athletic complex, weighing natural grass versus synthetic turf due to cost and environmental concerns. Superintendent Meni also delivered the State of the Schools address, detailing district performance, demographics, and commitment to diversity and inclusion.

title: January Regular Meeting
blurb: The school board extensively debated the SPHS Athletic Complex's future, considering artificial turf versus natural grass amidst public and board concerns, and discussed moving the 2026 graduation venue to the Cross Insurance Arena. Other agenda items included recognizing staff retirements, student achievements, and updates on bond-funded projects.

title: Special Meeting
blurb: The school board held a workshop on the future of the South Portland High School athletic complex, discussing natural grass versus synthetic turf options and a new, scaled-back synthetic turf proposal. The Board also unanimously denied a grievance from the South Portland Education Support Professionals Association.

title: December Regular Meeting
blurb: The South Portland Board of Education welcomed a new member and heard detailed reports on the district's successful efforts to reduce chronic absenteeism, the rapid growth and funding challenges of the Adult Education program, a proposal for a new K-4 math curriculum, and ongoing mental and behavioral health initiatives.

title: Technology & AI Policy Discussion
blurb: The board recognized a departing member and celebrated a student-led scholarship initiative for study abroad programs. Key discussions included changing the snow day policy to eliminate remote days and considering a new venue for high school graduation to accommodate more families.

title: Back to School & Equity Report
blurb: The board confronted a community in crisis, dedicating a significant portion of the meeting to discussing student mental health and suicide prevention in response to recent student deaths. The superintendent outlined a multi-faceted plan, while parents and board members made emotional pleas for urgent, expert-led intervention.

title: Opening of School Year
blurb: The school board reviewed successful student and staff summer programs, discussed extensive safety upgrades, and outlined district goals for the upcoming school year, including a new focus on strategic planning and reconfiguration.

title: July Regular Meeting
blurb: The board reviewed updates from the AI Steering Committee and positive student data from the high school. The main action was voting to send three bond referenda to the city council for facility improvements, including security upgrades, deferred maintenance, and a controversial renovation of the high school stadium complex featuring a synthetic turf field.

title: June Regular Meeting
blurb: The board celebrated numerous student achievements, including state championships for the track team, and discussed a potential $17 million bond for district-wide facility improvements, debating the environmental impact of a proposed artificial turf field.

title: Board Workshop and Special Meeting
blurb: The South Portland Board of Education held a special meeting to approve key personnel appointments, including a new principal for the high school and a new district-wide Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion. The board also entered an executive session to discuss collective bargaining with service employees.

title: FY2025 Budget Vote
blurb: The board celebrated numerous student and staff achievements, including the Top 20 Scholars of 2024, before unanimously passing the FY2025 budget. A significant portion of the meeting was dedicated to a complex and divided debate on the path forward for elementary school reconfiguration, ultimately resulting in votes to hire a consultant for analysis and establish a regular review of attendance zones.

title: April Regular Meeting
blurb: The board recognized outstanding staff and approved a revised FY25 budget, which included funding for a new, debated mental health coordinator position. A lengthy workshop followed, focusing on the elementary school boundaries and configuration steering committee's recommendations to address significant inequities across the district's schools.

title: Budget Workshop III
blurb: The Board of Education unanimously approved the FY2025 budget after a final presentation from the Superintendent, which also included discussions on a new partnership with JMG for Extended Learning Opportunities and addressing equity concerns in athletics.

title: Budget Workshop II
blurb: The Board held a budget workshop for the FY2025 budget, featuring presentations from the Special Education, Adult Education, Athletics, Technology, and Operations departments. The Superintendent announced a plan to retain an SPHS art teacher position while also committing to continue the popular Extended Learning Opportunities (ELO) program despite the loss of grant funding for its coordinator.

title: Budget Workshop I
blurb: The board held its first FY2025 budget workshop, where the Superintendent detailed a $69.5M proposal shaped by the loss of federal COVID funds. The meeting included extensive presentations on the district's Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS) and featured public comment urging the board to retain a high school art teacher position slated for elimination.

title: March Regular Meeting
blurb: The board celebrated the state champion SPHS Boys' Indoor Track team and received the Superintendent's proposed $69.4 million FY2025 budget, which represents a 3.82% school tax rate increase while navigating the loss of federal funds.

title: February Regular Meeting
blurb: The board addressed the resignation of DEI Coordinator Mohammed Abbi Hadley, condemning the racism that led to his departure, and received a detailed report from the Elementary Boundaries and Configuration Steering Committee highlighting significant inequities across elementary schools and proposing both short and long-term solutions.

title: State of the Schools
blurb: The board reviewed the annual State of the Schools report, which detailed significant demographic shifts, student achievement data, and school climate survey results. The meeting also addressed the recent resignation of the DEI director and concluded with a student and staff video on belonging.

title: January Regular Meeting
blurb: The South Portland Board of Education celebrated School Board Recognition Month with student artwork and heard updates on the FY25 budget process and school safety initiatives. The board also approved several policies and was urged by a citizen to prepare for upcoming discussions on district reconfiguration.
